name: grapix
description: GrapiX broadcast graphics platform: Editor, Playout and the standalone Render Engine.

scripts.build: npm run clean:dist && npm run build:shared && npm run build:editor && npm run build:playout && npm run stage:runtime
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck -w @grapix/shared-workspace && npm run typecheck -w @grapix/editor-workspace && npm run typecheck -w @grapix/playout-workspace
scripts.test: npm run test:shared && npm run test:editor && npm run test:playout
scripts.ship: npm run build && set CI=true&& npm run build -w @grapix/desktop-tauri && npm run build -w @grapix/playout-desktop
scripts.ship:editor: npm run build && set CI=true&& npm run build -w @grapix/desktop-tauri
scripts.ship:playout: npm run build && set CI=true&& npm run build -w @grapix/playout-desktop
scripts.certify:ae-runtime-fixtures: npm --prefix Playout/services/playout-control run build && sh tools/certification/ae-runtime-fixtures/run-edge-corpus.sh compare && sh tools/certification/ae-runtime-fixtures/run-lower-third.sh

//overrides: One copy of React, and one copy of its types, across the whole workspace. Two copies are not merely wasteful: hoisted packages (lucide-react, dockview-react) resolve the root copy, so they build elements with one React while an app renders them with the other — which surfaced as `Objects are not valid as a React child` from react-dom/server the moment the apps moved to 19. Two copies of the types fail the same way at compile time, because each declares its own `ReactNode`.
//devDependencies: React is declared at the root as well as in each app because hoisted packages (zustand, lucide-react, dockview-react) resolve it from here. Without a root copy they cannot find React at all; with a root copy at a *different* major they build elements the apps cannot render. So it is pinned to the same major as the apps, and `overrides` above keeps every transitive request on it.
